advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Harden the construct-uniqueness guard to detect a multi-line raw `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]` repo-root fallback (e.g. scan file text with re.DOTALL, not per-line).
evidence: The loop applies `pattern.search(line)` per individual line: `for lineno, line in enumerate(py.read_text().splitlines(), start=1):`
The formatter/black may wrap a reintroduced assignment across lines, in which case neither line alone contains both `repo_root` and the Path idiom, so `search` misses.
`for lineno, line in enumerate(py.read_text().splitlines(), start=1):` — no `encoding=` argument
Contrast with the deliberate use elsewhere in the same change: `cfg.write_text("# stand-in installed module\n", encoding="utf-8")`
advisory.finding: The construct-uniqueness guard regex requires `repo_root` and the `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[` idiom to appear on the SAME source line (single-line regex, no re.DOTALL / multiline join). A reintroduced raw package-location fallback split across two lines (e.g. `repo_root = (` newline `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4])`) would evade the guard, so the regression test is weaker than its docstring claims ("No rebar_reconciler module may derive its repo root from a raw ... fallback").
merged_from: The guard test reads reconciler source files with `py.read_text()` without an explicit `encoding=`, so it relies on the platform default locale encoding. On a non-UTF-8 default (e.g. some CI/Windows locales) a source file containing non-ASCII bytes could raise UnicodeDecodeError, turning a scope-guard test into a spurious failure.
scenarios: A future edit reintroduces the raw fallback but the assignment is line-wrapped, defeating the single-line regex.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep guard with a behavioral assertion that fetcher.py's repo_root=None default actually resolves via config.reconciler_repo_root() (e.g. monkeypatch config.reconciler_repo_root to a sentinel and assert fetch_snapshot/compute_snapshot use it), so the guard survives a reformat and detects a real routing regression.
evidence: for py in sorted(recon_dir.rglob("*.py")): for lineno, line in enumerate(py.read_text().splitlines(), ...): if pattern.search(line): offenders.append(...)

This greps executable SOURCE CODE UNDER TEST (not a non-executable instruction artifact), so the Rule-5 structural-artifact exception does not apply; it tests the implementation text, breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor, and passes despite a broken resolver (refactoring-violation + regression-blindness criteria).
advisory.finding: The construct-uniqueness guard test asserts against the TEXT of source code under test (a regex grep over reconciler_reconciler/*.py) rather than observable behavior, making it a source-grepping change-detector. The regex `repo_root\b.*Path\(__file__\)\.resolve\(\)\.parents\[` only matches when both tokens fall on the SAME line, so a behavior-preserving reformat (splitting the fallback across two lines, or renaming the local) evades detection with no behavior change, and the test stays green even if reconciler_repo_root() is wrong.

coaching.coaching: Delete the change-detector / tautological test the source-grepping construct-uniqueness guard test; do not re-pin it to the new source text — a test that only mirrors the implementation asserts nothing.
coaching.subject: the source-grepping construct-uniqueness guard test
